successors.name: Achaemenid Empire
successors.text: the Phoenician coast from Arwad to Mount Carmel, one satrapy of the Persian Empire

ledger.x: c. 1150 BC: the Phoenician city-states stand free after the Bronze Age collapse. The page says the Late Bronze Age collapse (1200–1150) severely weakened or destroyed Egypt and the Hittites while the Phoenician cities survived, that Tyre, Sidon and Byblos kept their independence by 1230, and that the core area…
738 BC: Tyre and Byblos become Assyrian tributaries.
609 BC (bridged): the tribute to Assyria ends with the empire; neo-assyrian-empire /ledger/58 and neo-babylonian-empire /ledger/3 send the west to Babylon that year.
573 BC: the siege of Tyre ends.
573 BC: Tyre and the Phoenician cities pass under Babylonian rule.
539 BC: Cyrus the Great takes Babylon and the Levant becomes one satrapy.
539 BC: the Phoenician city-states pass under Persian rule.
539 BC: Babylonian rule ends when Cyrus takes Babylon.

wars.name: Assyrian annexation of northern Phoenicia (Tiglath-Pileser III)
wars.outcome: Northern Phoenicia annexed; Tyre and Byblos left as tributary states.

wars.name: Tiglath-Pileser III's Levant campaigns and the capture of Tyre
wars.outcome: Pattin and northern Phoenicia annexed in 738 (provinces Kullania, Hatarikka, Simirra), Byblos and Tyre paying tribute; in 732 Damascus fell and the page also records that Tyre was captured, without saying whether it was annexed or left as a vassal.

wars.name: Sargon II's siege of Tyre
wars.outcome: Sargon II besieges Tyre and crushes the rebellion; no territory changes.

wars.name: Esarhaddon's capture of Sidon
wars.outcome: Sidon taken in 677, its king executed in 676, the city made an Assyrian province; two Sidonian cities given to Baal of Tyre.

wars.name: Nebuchadnezzar II's siege of Tyre
wars.outcome: A thirteen-year siege; the city was not destroyed and came under Babylonian rule in 572 (Tyre page).

wars.name: Persian conquest of the Levant
wars.outcome: Cyrus takes Babylon; the Levant is consolidated into a single satrapy and the Phoenician area divided into four vassal kingdoms.

certainty.note: The city-states' territories were thin coastal strips between the sea and the mountains and no treaty or survey line survives; the western colonies are points, not areas.
